title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol: Biel — end loved before means; faith gift prepared with life destinated
pass_a_gloss: For Biel rightly, The end is loved before the means, which is loved on account of the end: because the love of the end is in some way the cause of the love of all those things which are unto the end. For since faith is a gift of God, bringing eternal life to the believer, who would dare say that this gift was prepared and gifted to Peter or Paul, eternal life not yet destinated to them? as if God had not destinated the benefit which will arise from his gift to him whom he willed to enrich with the same gift before others.
pass_b_english: Biel is right: the end is loved before the means loved for the end's sake — love of the end is in some way cause of loving all that is unto the end. Since faith is God's gift bringing eternal life to the believer, who would dare say that gift was prepared and given to Peter or Paul while eternal life was not yet destinated to them? As if God had not destinated the benefit arising from his gift to the one he willed to enrich with that gift before others.
source_text: Recte enim Biel, Prius diligitur finis quam medium, quod propter finem diligitur: quia dilectio finis est aliquo modo causa dilectionis eorum omnium quae sunt ad finem. Cum enim fides sit donum Dei, vitam aeternam credenti apportans, quis audeat dicere hoc donum fuisse Petro aut Paulo praeparatum et donatum, vita aeterna nondum illis destinata? quasi Deus beneficium, quod ex suo dono orietur, non destinaverit ei, quem eodem dono prae aliis voluerit locupletare.
